references.text: God blessed the humans and said they should be fruitful and multiply – marriage and procreation belong to this world's order, which Jesus refers to with the expression "children of this age" ([ref:1 Mos 1:28|Genesis 1:28]).

The institution of marriage in the creation account, where man and woman are united into one flesh. Jesus points out that this is an arrangement that applies to "this age" ([ref:1 Mos 2:22-24|Genesis 2:22-24]).
Matthew's parallel passage where Jesus says that in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God's angels in heaven ([ref:Matt 22:30|Matthew 22:30]).
Mark's parallel passage which also recounts Jesus' answer that those who are raised neither marry nor are given in marriage ([ref:Mark 12:25|Mark 12:25]).

Paul speaks about the time being short and that those who have wives should live as if they did not, for this world's form is passing away. This reflects Jesus' distinction between the arrangements of this age and the coming one ([ref:1 Kor 7:29-31|1 Corinthians 7:29-31]).

Paul distinguishes between "this age" and "the coming one", which corresponds to Jesus' expression "children of this world" in contrast to those who are worthy of the coming world ([ref:Ef 1:21|Ephesians 1:21]).
Jesus uses the expression "children of this world" (οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου) also in the parable of the unjust steward, where he contrasts them with "children of light" ([ref:Luk 16:8|Luke 16:8]).

The continuation of Jesus' answer, where he explains that those who are worthy of the coming world and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor die, but are like angels ([ref:Luk 20:35-36|Luke 20:35-36]).
